content: Eating patterns describe the habitual selection of foods and beverages consumed on a regular basis. These patterns may include specific dietary approaches, such as the Mediterranean diet or the DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) diet. However, no single dietary pattern is universally optimal for everyone. It is crucial to customize these dietary plans to meet an individual’s unique needs, preferences, and access to food in order to effectively manage diabetes. Meal planning plays a critical role in diabetes care. A registered dietitian nutritionist (RDN) is indispensable in assisting individuals with diabetes to create a sustainable meal plan that aligns with their personal health goals and medical conditions. Evidence-based dietary recommendations emphasize prioritizing non-starchy vegetables, whole grains, nuts, seeds, and low-fat dairy products. At the same time, it is important to limit the consumption of processed foods and added sugars.
